title: Restaurant Reviews Dashboard
text:
This project explores how customer sentiment and review volume evolved over time for various restaurants. We used natural language processing (NLP) to extract sentiment from review text and visualized how it correlated with rating trends.




Pandas for data cleaning
TextBlob for sentiment scoring
Matplotlib for visualizations
WordCloud for text frequency visualization
Streamlit (optional) for interactive dashboard








Rating and Sentiment Over Time









Number of Reviews Over Time






We visualized the most commonly used words across all reviews to identify recurring themes in customer feedback.

This project shows how customer feedback evolves and how NLP can provide actionable business insights. This type of analysis is useful for marketing, operations, and quality control in customer-facing industries.

title: Loan Approval Prediction
text:
Can we predict whether a loan application will be approved based on applicant information? This project simulates how financial institutions can use data science to improve decision-making in the lending process.




The dataset (Kaggle Playground Series S4E10) includes:

Applicant age, income and home ownership
Employment length
Loan purpose (intent), grade and amount
Interest rate and loan-to-income ratio
Credit history length and prior defaults
Loan status (approved / not approved), the target

After preprocessing, we were left with a clean dataset ready for modeling.




































Key insights discovered:

Debt consolidation, medical, and home improvement loans had the highest approval rates.
Venture loans had the lowest approval rate, indicating higher perceived risk.
Approved applicants tended to have slightly lower median incomes, although the income range overlaps heavily.
The income distribution is heavily right-skewed, requiring log scaling for meaningful visualization.

Visuals like histograms, boxplots, and bar charts were used to uncover these patterns.









Accuracy: 0.91
Precision: 0.77
Recall: 0.54



















Accuracy: 0.95
Precision: 0.92
Recall: 0.72
















We compared two models:

Logistic Regression (baseline)
Random Forest

The Random Forest model delivered the best overall performance.
Final Metrics (Random Forest):

Accuracy: 0.95
Precision: 0.92
Recall: 0.72

Feature importance analysis highlighted loan_percent_income, loan_int_rate, and person_income as the top predictors.






The Random Forest model achieved the best performance with strong accuracy and balanced metrics.
Loan-to-income ratio, interest rate, and income were the top predictors, according to feature importance.
Precision (92%) suggests the model reliably predicts approved loans, and recall (72%) shows good coverage of actual approvals.
To improve the model:

Consider using external credit data or employment verification APIs
Explore class imbalance handling (e.g., SMOTE, weighted loss)
Experiment with gradient boosting models for potential gains






📂 View the code for this page on GitHub
📂 R version of this analysis (logistic regression + k-NN)
📁 Dataset: Kaggle Playground Series S4E10, Loan Approval Prediction

text:

title: Netflix User Segmentation
text:
This project explores how we can segment Netflix-style users based on their viewing and rating behavior. We use unsupervised learning techniques (K-Means and PCA) to uncover distinct audience groups from the MovieLens 100K dataset, a popular proxy for streaming behavior.




Pandas for data wrangling
Scikit-learn for K-Means clustering & PCA
Matplotlib for visualizations
StandardScaler for normalization





We used K-Means clustering on normalized user behavior (e.g., avg rating, rating frequency, rating consistency). PCA was applied to reduce dimensions and visualize user segments.



User Clusters






Here’s the number of users that fell into each cluster group:



Cluster Sizes






Some clusters tend to rate movies more positively than others. This view reveals behavioral differences between user types.



Average Rating by Cluster







Cluster 1 contains high-frequency raters with consistently high ratings — likely loyal or engaged users
Cluster 2 includes viewers with low average ratings — possibly critics or picky watchers
Cluster 3 has moderate activity and average rating variance — casual or balanced users
Cluster 0 users are active but inconsistent — might reflect binge-watchers or exploratory viewers

These segments can help streaming platforms personalize recommendations, manage churn risk, or optimize engagement strategies.




Code used for clustering and visualizations: netflix_clustering.py




This project demonstrates how clustering can uncover meaningful user segments from real viewing data. Streaming platforms can use these insights to improve personalization, understand viewer behavior, and enhance user retention.
